paragraphs: Tutor Perini Corporation (together with its consolidated subsidiaries, "Tutor Perini," the "Company," "we," "us," and "our," unless the context indicates otherwise) is a leading construction company offering diversified general contracting, construction management and design-build services to private customers and public agencies throughout the world. The Company was formed through the 2008 merger between Tutor-Saliba Corporation and Perini Corporation ("Perini") and our legacy dates to 1894, when Perini's predecessor businesses began providing construction services. Our corporate headquarters are in Los Angeles (Sylmar), California, and we have various other principal offices throughout the United States and its territories (see Item 2. Properties for a listing of our major facilities). Our common stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "TPC." We are incorporated in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.

We are a recognized leader in the construction industry and have built a solid reputation for executing large, complex projects while adhering to strict safety and quality control standards. We offer general contracting, pre-construction planning and comprehensive project management services, and have strong expertise in planning and delivering design-bid-build, design-build, construction management, and public-private partnership (P3) projects. We often utilize our resources and capabilities to self-perform multiple components of our projects, including earthwork, excavation, concrete forming and placement, steel erection, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), and fire protection. During 2025, we performed work on approximately 1,600 construction projects.

We are recognized as one of the leading civil contractors in the United States, as evidenced by our performance on several of the country's largest mass-transit and transportation projects, such as Newark Liberty International Airport's AirTrain Replacement project and new Terminal A ("Newark Airport Terminal A"), various components of the East Side Access project, along with the Midtown Bus Terminal Replacement - Phase 1 project, and the Manhattan Tunnel project, all in New York, the Minneapolis Southwest Light Rail project (also known as the METRO Green Line Extension), the California High-Speed Rail System, the Alaskan Way Viaduct Replacement (the "SR 99") project in Seattle, major portions of the Red Line and Purple Line subway segments of the Los Angeles Metro system, the San Francisco Central Subway extension to Chinatown, and the City Center Guideway and Stations project in Hawaii. We are also recognized as one of the major building contractors in the United States, as evidenced by our performance on several of the country's largest building development projects, including Hudson Yards and the new Brooklyn and Manhattan Jail projects in New York City, the CityCenter complex and the Cosmopolitan Resort and Casino, both in Las Vegas, as well as several major technology, healthcare and educational facilities in California for prominent customers.

Our strengths and expertise in the construction of civil and building infrastructure projects have been augmented by our vertical integration capabilities, which we established more than a decade ago through the acquisitions of various business entities specializing in electrical, mechanical, plumbing, HVAC and other services that enhance our market capabilities and expand our geographic presence. Our vertical integration capabilities, which also involve close interactions between our Civil and Building segment resources on large, complex projects, are a competitive advantage that allow us to self-perform a greater amount of work than our competitors. These capabilities also increase our competitiveness in bidding and our efficiency in managing and executing large projects, and provide us with significant cross-selling opportunities across a broad geographic footprint.
Our business is conducted through three segments: Civil, Building and Specialty Contractors.

Our Civil segment specializes in public works construction and the replacement and reconstruction of infrastructure across several major geographic regions of the United States. Our civil contracting services include construction and rehabilitation of highways, bridges, tunnels, mass-transit systems, military and other government facilities, and water management and wastewater treatment facilities.

The Civil segment is composed of the heavy civil construction operations of Tutor Perini and its subsidiaries, Black Construction, Frontier-Kemper Constructors ("Frontier-Kemper"), Lunda Construction and Becho. Our heavy civil units operate primarily on the West and East Coasts of the United States and are engaged in a variety of large mass-transit, tunneling, bridge and highway projects. Black Construction is the largest contractor in Guam and provides a variety of predominantly heavy civil, building, mechanical and electrical construction services throughout the Asia-Pacific region and in other strategic military locations. Frontier-Kemper is a heavy civil contractor engaged in the construction of tunnels for highways, railroads, subways and rapid transit systems; the construction of shafts and other facilities for water supply, wastewater transport and hydroelectric projects; and the development and equipping of mines with innovative hoisting, elevator and vertical conveyance systems. Lunda Construction is a heavy civil contractor specializing in the construction, rehabilitation and maintenance of bridges, railroads and other civil structures throughout the United States. Becho is engaged in drilling, foundation and excavation support for shoring, bridges, piers, roads and highway projects, primarily in the southwestern United States.

Our Civil segment's customers primarily award contracts through one of two methods: the traditional public "competitive bid" method, in which price is the major determining factor, or through a best value proposal, where contracts are awarded based on a combination of technical qualifications, proposed project team, schedule, past performance on similar projects and price.

Traditionally, our Civil segment's customers require each contractor to pre-qualify for construction business by meeting criteria that include technical capabilities and financial strength. Our financial strength, outstanding record of performance on challenging civil works projects, and vertical integration capabilities often enable us to pre-qualify for projects in situations where smaller, less diversified contractors are unable to meet the qualification requirements. We believe this is a competitive advantage that allows us to self-perform a greater amount of work and makes us an ideal lead contractor for the largest, most complex infrastructure projects and on prestigious design-build, design-build-operate-maintain and public-private partnership projects.

We have been active in civil construction since 1894 and believe we have a particular expertise in large, complex civil construction projects. We are currently working on or have completed some of the most significant civil construction projects in the United States. For example, we are working on the first phase of the California High-Speed Rail project, the Purple Line Segments 2 and 3 subway expansion projects in Los Angeles, the Minneapolis Southwest Light Rail project, the City Center Guideway and Stations project in Honolulu, and the Midtown Bus Terminal Replacement, the Newark AirTrain Replacement, and the Kensico-Eastview Connection Tunnel projects, all in New York. In addition, we have completed other major projects, including various components of the East Side Access project in New York City; the Newark Airport Terminal A project; the San Francisco Central Subway extension to Chinatown; the SR 99 project in Seattle; the platform over the eastern rail yard at Hudson Yards in New York City; the rehabilitation of the Verrazano-Narrows Bridge in New York City; and runway reconstruction projects at John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York, Los Angeles International Airport and Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport.

We believe the Civil segment provides us with significant opportunities for growth due to the condition of existing infrastructure coupled with large government funding sources dedicated to the replacement and reconstruction of aging U.S. infrastructure. In addition, infrastructure programs generally garner popular, bipartisan support from the public and elected officials due to their lasting economic benefits, including significant job creation. Funding for major Civil segment infrastructure projects is typically provided through a combination of one or more of the following: local, regional, state and federal loans and grants; other direct allocations sourced through tax revenue; bonds; user fees; and, for certain projects, private capital.

The bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (the "Bipartisan Infrastructure Law") was enacted into law in November 2021 and provided for $1.2 trillion of federal infrastructure funding, including $550 billion in new spending for improvements to the country's surface-transportation network and enhancements to core infrastructure. The Bipartisan Infrastructure Law initiated the largest federal investment in public transit ever, the single largest dedicated bridge investment since the construction of the interstate highway system and the largest federal investment in passenger rail since the creation of Amtrak, all in addition to providing for regular annual spending for numerous infrastructure projects. This significant incremental funding is anticipated to be spent over the 10 years from its enactment through 2031, and much of it is allocated for investment in end markets that are directly aligned with our market focus. Accordingly, we believe that this significant funding has benefited, and will continue to favorably impact, our current work and prospective opportunities over the next decade. While the current funding window for the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law closes on September 30, 2026, we believe that Congress recognizes the long-term nature of infrastructure work and is already engaged in the legislative process to secure future funding beyond that date, although any amount and composition of such future funding is yet to be determined. In addition, various existing projects and future project opportunities in Guam and the Indo-Pacific region are being funded by the U.S. government's Pacific Deterrence Initiative, which provides substantial multi-year funding to support significant improvements that enhance the U.S. military's infrastructure and readiness.

Our Building segment has significant experience providing services to several specialized building markets for private and public works customers, including hospitality and gaming, transportation, healthcare, commercial offices, government facilities, sports and entertainment, education, correctional and detention facilities, biotech, pharmaceutical, industrial and technology. We believe the success of the Building segment results from our proven ability to manage and perform large, complex projects with aggressive fast-track schedules, elaborate designs, and advanced mechanical, electrical and life safety systems, while providing accurate budgeting and strict quality control. We believe our strong reputation, long-standing customer relationships, competitive pricing and significant level of repeat and referral business have enabled us to achieve a leading position in the marketplace.

We are a recognized leader in the hospitality and gaming market, specializing in the construction of high-end resorts and casinos. We work with hotel operators, Native American tribal councils, developers and architectural firms to provide diversified construction services to meet the challenges of new construction and renovation of hotel and resort properties. We believe that our reputation for completing projects on time is a significant competitive advantage in this market, as any delay in project completion could result in significant loss of revenue for the customer.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Operations
If we are unable to accurately estimate contract risks, revenue or costs, we may incur a loss or achieve lower than anticipated profit.
Our contracts often require us to perform extra work beyond the initial project scope, which can result in disputes or claims and adversely affect our working capital, profits and cash flows.
Economic factors, such as inflation, tariffs, the timing of new awards, or the pace of project execution, have resulted and may continue to result in losses or lower than anticipated profit.
Our actual results could differ from the estimates and assumptions used to prepare our financial statements.
A significant slowdown or decline in economic conditions, such as those presented during a recession, could adversely affect our operations.

The construction services industry is highly schedule driven, and our failure to meet the schedule requirements of our contracts could adversely affect our reputation and/or expose us to financial liability.

Decreases or delays in the level of federal, state and local government spending for infrastructure and other public projects could adversely affect the number of projects available to us in the future.
Systems and information technology interruption and breaches in data security and/or privacy could adversely impact our ability to operate and negatively impact our operating results.
Weather conditions and other events outside our control can significantly affect our revenue and profitability.
We are subject to risks related to government contracts (including government shutdowns and funding considerations) and related procurement regulations.

Our international operations expose us to economic, political, regulatory and other risks, as well as uncertainty related to U.S. government funding, which could adversely affect our revenue and earnings.
Our participation in construction joint ventures exposes us to liability and/or harm to our reputation for failures by our partners.
We may not fully realize the revenue value reported in our backlog due to cancellations or reductions in scope, including as a result of government-related mandates.
Competition for new project awards is intense, and our failure to compete effectively could reduce our market share and profits.
We could be adversely affected by violations of the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and similar worldwide anti-bribery laws.
Public health crises, such as COVID-19, have adversely impacted, and could in the future adversely impact, our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Physical and regulatory risks related to climate change could have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Risks Related to Our Capital Structure
An inability to obtain bonding could have a negative impact on our operations and results.
We have a substantial amount of indebtedness with restrictive covenants which could adversely affect our financial position and prevent us from fulfilling our obligations under our debt agreements.
Downgrades in our credit ratings could have a material adverse effect on our business and financial condition.
Risk Related to Our Stock Ownership
Our executive chairman could exert influence over the Company due to his position and significant ownership interest.
General Risk Factors
The market price of our common stock may fluctuate significantly, which could result in substantial losses for shareholders and subject us to litigation.
We cannot guarantee the timing, amount, or payment of dividends on our common stock or that we will repurchase our common stock pursuant to our stock repurchase program.
paragraphs: We are subject to a number of known and unknown risks and uncertainties that could have a material adverse effect on our operations. Set forth below, and elsewhere in this report, are descriptions of the material risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from the results contemplated by the forward-looking statements contained in this report and could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

Accounting for contract-related revenue and costs requires management to make significant estimates and assumptions that may change substantially throughout the project lifecycle, which has previously resulted, and in the future could result, in a material impact to our consolidated financial statements. In addition, cost overruns, including unanticipated cost increases on fixed price contracts and guaranteed maximum price contracts, have previously resulted, and in the future may result, in lower profits or losses.

We are involved in a significant number of legal proceedings which, if determined unfavorable to us, could adversely affect our financial results and/or cash flows, harm our reputation and/or preclude us from bidding on future projects. We also may invest significant working capital on projects while legal proceedings are being settled.

We are involved in various lawsuits, including the legal proceedings described under Note 8 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements. Litigation is inherently uncertain, and it is not possible to accurately predict what the final outcome will be of any legal proceeding. We must make certain assumptions and rely on estimates, which are inherently subject to risks and uncertainties, regarding potential outcomes of legal proceedings in order to determine an appropriate contingent liability and charge to income. Any adverse legal proceeding outcome or settlement that is materially different from our expectations and estimates could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. This may include requiring us to record an expense or reduce revenue that we previously recorded based on our expectations or estimates, requiring us to pay damages or reducing cash collections that we had expected to receive. For example, in October 2024, we received an unexpected adverse arbitration decision on a legacy dispute related to a completed Civil segment bridge project in California that resulted in a non-cash charge of $101.6 million, which we are appealing. In addition, any future adverse judgments could harm our reputation and negatively impact our ability to win future projects.

We may bring claims against project owners for additional cost exceeding the contract price or for amounts not included in the original contract price. When these types of events occur and unresolved claims are pending, we may invest significant working capital in projects to cover cost overruns pending the resolution of the relevant claims. A failure to promptly recover on these types of claims has had and could continue to have a material adverse effect on our liquidity and financial results and could result in further legal proceedings.

Our contracts often require us to perform extra work beyond the initial project scope as directed by the customer even if the customer has not agreed in advance on the scope and/or price of the work to be performed. This process has resulted and in the future could result in disputes or claims over whether the work performed is beyond the scope of work directed by the customer and/or exceeds the price the customer is willing to pay for the work performed, which has resulted in significant cash flow constraints in the past. To the extent we do not recover our costs for this work or there are delays in the recovery of these costs, whether as a result of an unfavorable outcome in a litigation or arbitration or as a result of a settlement in which we agree to accept less than we had expected, our working capital, profits and cash flows have been and could continue to be adversely impacted.

paragraphs: Consolidated revenue for 2025 was $5.5 billion, up 28% compared to $4.3 billion for 2024. The Company experienced strong growth in all three segments in 2025, primarily driven by increased project execution activities on certain newer, larger and higher-margin projects, all of which have significant scope of work remaining. These projects are in the early stages and are expected to ramp up substantially over the next several years.

Income from construction operations for 2025 was $232.0 million, a dramatic improvement compared to a loss from construction operations of $103.8 million for 2024. The increase in income from construction operations in 2025 was primarily due to contributions related to an overall net increase in project execution activities that totaled $172.1 million and a lower amount of net unfavorable adjustments in 2025 driven by changes in the estimate at completion for various projects, including: 1) impacts from improved productivity and efficiencies on certain projects, net of project charges, which had an aggregate net favorable impact of $104.3 million in 2025 compared to a net unfavorable impact of $36.4 million in 2024; 2) certain legal judgments or decisions that had net unfavorable impacts totaling $32.5 million in 2025 compared to $167.7 million in 2024; and 3) temporary aggregate negative project adjustments of $78.7 million in 2025 compared to $97.2 million in 2024 due to both the successful negotiation of significant lower margin (and lower risk) change orders and increases in unapproved work on various projects, the temporary impacts to earnings of which are expected to reverse themselves over the remaining lives of the projects. The improvement was partially offset by the impact of various settlements that had a net unfavorable impact of $61.8 million in 2025 compared to $45.8 million in 2024. The significant adjustments in 2025 and 2024 resulting from the above items are discussed in more detail in Results of Segment Operations.

Furthermore, income from construction operations for the year ended December 31, 2025 was negatively impacted by share-based compensation expense of $150.0 million compared to share-based compensation expense of $40.4 million in 2024. The increase in share-based compensation expense in 2025 was primarily due to a substantial increase of 176.9% in the Company's stock price during 2025, which impacted the fair value of liability-classified awards. These liability-classified awards are remeasured at fair value at the end of each reporting period with the change recognized in earnings. These types of awards were issued in past years as a short-term solution to deal with a depleted share pool under the Tutor Perini Corporation Omnibus Incentive Plan (the "Plan") and a low stock price. The Company currently projects a decrease in share-based compensation expense in 2026 and a much more significant decrease in 2027 as certain such awards have vested and most of the remaining liability-classified awards will vest by the end of 2026. After the Company's shareholders approved additional shares under the Plan in May 2025, the Company stopped issuing liability-classified, long-term incentive compensation awards, which will help to reduce future earnings volatility.
The effective income tax rate for 2025 was 30.0% compared to 29.3% for 2024. See Corporate, Tax and Other Matters below for a discussion of the change in the effective tax rate.

Diluted earnings per common share for 2025 was $1.51 compared to diluted loss per common share of $3.13 for 2024. Adjusted diluted earnings per common share, which is a non-GAAP financial measure and excludes share-based compensation expense (and the associated tax benefit) for 2025 was $4.29, compared to an adjusted diluted loss per common share of $2.37 for 2024. The improvement for 2025 was primarily due to the factors discussed above that resulted in the change in income (loss) from construction operations for such period. Refer to the Non-GAAP Financial Measures section below for further information and a reconciliation of the Company's financial results reported under generally accepted accounting principles in the United States ("GAAP") to the reported adjusted results.

The Company generated record cash flow from operations of $748.1 million in 2025 largely driven by collections from newer and ongoing projects and, to a much lesser extent, from collections related to recent dispute resolutions. The Company utilized some of its cash flow from operations in 2025 to voluntarily prepay its outstanding Term Loan B debt of $121.9 million.

Consolidated new awards in 2025 were $7.4 billion compared to $12.8 billion in 2024. The Civil and Building segments were the primary contributors to the new awards activity in 2025. Significant new awards and contract adjustments in 2025 included the $1.87 billion Midtown Bus Terminal Replacement - Phase 1 project in New York; the $1.18 billion Manhattan Tunnel project in New York; a healthcare facility project in California valued at approximately $1 billion; a $538 million healthcare project in California; $241 million of additional funding for the Apra Harbor Waterfront Repairs project in Guam; a $182 million military defense project in Guam; a $155 million education facility project in California; $131 million of additional funding for an electrical project in Texas; and another electrical project in Texas valued at more than $100 million. The Company has continued to be successful in winning its share of major new project opportunities due to a combination of its strategic bidding approach and favorable market dynamics, including limited competition in select markets for some of the larger projects. This environment, which is supported by strong public funding and demand, has allowed the Company to differentiate itself and deliver compelling proposals that align with the customer's goals and expectations. The Company expects that this environment will continue for the foreseeable future.

Consolidated backlog as of December 31, 2025 was $20.6 billion, up 10% compared to $18.7 billion as of December 31, 2024. As of December 31, 2025, the mix of backlog by segment was 49% for Civil, 36% for Building and 15% for Specialty Contractors, compared to 47% for Civil, 38% for Building and 15% for Specialty Contractors at the end of 2024.

Most projects in the Civil segment's backlog typically convert to revenue over a period of three to five years and in the Building and Specialty Contractors segments over a period of one to three years. Certain larger projects across all three segments may extend over a longer duration. We estimate that approximately $6 billion, or approximately 29%, of our backlog as of December 31, 2025 will be recognized as revenue in 2026.

paragraphs: Tutor Perini Corporation（含其合併子公司，簡稱「Tutor Perini」，「本公司」、「我們」、「我們」及「我們的」，除非文意另有明示）為一領導的建設公司，提供多樣化的總承包、建設管理及設計建造服務，服務對象為全球的私人客戶與政府機構。本公司係透過2008年Tutor-Saliba Corporation與Perini Corporation（簡稱「Perini」）的合併所成立，我們的歷史可追溯至1894年，當時Perini的前身企業開始提供建設服務。本公司總部設於洛杉磯（Sylmar），加州，並於美國及其屬地設有其他主要辦公室（詳見第2項財產，以取得我們主要設施清單）。我們的普通股於紐約證券交易所上市，代碼為「TPC」。本公司設立於馬薩諸塞州。

我們在建設產業中被視為領導者，並已建立穩固的聲譽，能執行大型、複雜的項目，同時遵守嚴格的安全與品質控制標準。我們提供總承包、預建設規劃及全面的項目管理服務，並在規劃與交付設計招標建造、設計建造、建設管理及公私合作（P3）項目方面具備強大的專業能力。我們經常運用自身資源與能力，自行執行多數項目零組件，包括土方工程、挖掘、混凝土製造與佈設、鋼結構安裝、電氣、機械、水管、暖通空調（HVAC）及防火保護。2025年，我們執行約1,600個建設項目。

我們被視為美國領先的土木承包商之一，這從我們在該國最大規模的通勤與交通項目上的表現可見一斑，例如紐約機場的AirTrain Replacement項目與新Terminal A（「紐約機場Terminal A」），東側通勤項目各項組成部分，以及Midtown Bus Terminal Replacement - Phase 1項目與Manhattan Tunnel項目，皆位於紐約； Minneapolis Southwest Light Rail項目（亦稱METRO Green Line Extension），加州高速鐵路系統，西雅圖的Alaskan Way Viaduct Replacement（簡稱「SR 99」）項目，洛杉磯地鐵紅線與紫線的多數路段，舊金山中央地鐵延伸至唐人街，以及夏威夷的City Center Guideway及車站項目。我們也被視為美國主要的建築承包商之一，這從我們在該國最大規模的建築開發項目上的表現可見一斑，包括紐約市的Hudson Yards與新布魯克林與曼哈頓監獄項目，拉斯維加斯的CityCenter複合體與Cosmopolitan度假村與賭場，以及加州為知名客戶建造的多個科技、醫療與教育設施。

我們在土木與建築基礎設施項目建設方面的優勢與專業能力，因我們建立的垂直整合能力而更上層樓，此能力係透過十多年來收購多家專門從事電氣、機械、水管、HVAC及其他服務的企業而建立，這些企業能提升我們的市場能力並擴展我們的地理佈局。我們的垂直整合能力，也涉及Civil與Building業務部門在大型、複雜項目上的密切合作，這是一項競爭優勢，使我們能比競爭對手執行更多工作。這些能力也提高我們在投標中的競爭力，並提升我們在管理與執行大型項目上的效率，同時為我們提供廣泛地理範圍內的重要交叉銷售機會。
我們的業務透過三個應報告分部進行：Civil、Building與Specialty Contractors。
我們的Civil分部專門從事公共工程建設與美國多個主要地理區域的基礎設施更換與重建。我們的土木承包服務包括高速公路、橋樑、隧道、大眾捷運系統、軍事及其他政府設施的建設與修復，以及水資源管理與污水處理設施。

Civil分部由Tutor Perini及其子公司Black Construction、Frontier-Kemper Constructors（簡稱「Frontier-Kemper」）、Lunda Construction與Becho的重體土木建設業務組成。我們的重體土木單位主要於美國東、西海岸進行業務，並參與多種大型大眾捷運、隧道、橋樑與高速公路項目。Black Construction為 Guam 最大的承包商，並在亞太地區及其他戰略軍事地點提供多樣化的重體土木、建築、機械與電氣建設服務。Frontier-Kemper為一家重體土木承包商，專門從事高速公路、鐵路、地鐵與快速運輸系統的隧道建設；水供應、污水運輸與水電工程的井道與其他設施建設；以及開發與裝備礦場，採用創新提升、電梯與垂直運輸系統。Lunda Construction為一家重體土木承包商，專門從事美國境內橋樑、鐵路及其他土木結構的建設、修復與維護。Becho從事鑽探、地基與挖掘支撐，用於支撐、橋樑、碼頭、道路與高速公路項目，主要位於美國西南部。
我們的Civil分部客戶主要透過兩種方式授予合約：傳統的公共「競標」方式，其中價格為主要決定因素，或透過最佳價值提案，其中合約依據技術資格、建議項目團隊、進度、類似項目過去表現與價格的組合來授予。

傳統上，我們的民用分部客戶要求每家承包商透過符合技術能力與財務實力等標準的條件，進行施工業務的預資格認證。我們的財務實力、在挑戰性民用工程專案中出色的履約紀錄，以及垂直整合能力，經常使我們能在小型、較不多元化的承包商無法符合資格要求的情況下，取得預資格認證。我們認為這是一項競爭優勢，使我們能執行更多工作，並成為最大、最複雜基礎建設專案的理想主承包商，以及在 prestigious design-build、design-build-operate-maintain 和 public-private partnership 專案中。

我們自 1894 年起積極參與民用建設，並認為我們在大型、複雜民用建設專案方面有特別的專業知識。我們目前正在進行或已完成美國一些最重要的民用建設專案。例如，我們正在進行加州高速鐵路專案的第一階段、洛杉磯 Purple Line Segments 2 和 3 地鐵擴建專案、明尼阿波利斯西南輕軌專案、火奴魯魯 City Center Guideway 和 Stations 專案、紐約的 Midtown Bus Terminal 替代專案、Newark AirTrain 替代專案，以及 Kensico-Eastview Connection Tunnel 專案。此外，我們已完成其他重大專案，包括紐約市 East Side Access 專案的多個組成部分；紐約 Newark Airport Terminal A 專案；舊金山中央地鐵延伸至 Chinatown；西雅圖 SR 99 專案；紐約市 Hudson Yards 東側車站上方的月臺；紐約市 Verrazano-Narrows 橋的整修；以及約翰·F·肯尼迪國際機場、洛杉磯國際機場和佛羅裏達州邁阿密-霍利迪斯普林斯國際機場的跑道重建專案。

我們認為民用分部為我們帶來了顯著的成長機會，這是因為現有基礎設施的狀態，加上專門用於替換和重建美國老化基礎設施的大量政府資金來源。此外，基礎設施計畫通常因其持久的經濟效益，包括大量就業機會，而獲得公眾和選舉人代表的廣泛、跨黨派支持。重大民用分部基礎設施專案的資金通常透過以下一種或多種方式提供：地方、區域、州和聯邦貸款和補助金；透過稅收收入直接分配的其他資金；債券；使用者費用；以及某些專案的私人資金。

跨黨派基礎建設投資與就業法案（"Bipartisan Infrastructure Law"）於 2021 年 11 月成為法律，並提供 1.2 兆美元的聯邦基礎設施資金，包括 5500 億美元的新支出，用於改善國家的地面交通網路和加強核心基礎設施。該法案啟動了歷史上最大的聯邦公共交通投資、自州際高速公路系統建設以來最大的專屬橋樑投資，以及自 Amtrak 創立以來最大的聯邦乘客鐵路投資，此外還提供多項基礎設施專案的定期年度支出。這筆顯著的額外資金預計將在法案通過後的 10 年內，即至 2031 年，逐步支出，其中大部分資金用於與我們市場重點直接對應的終端市場。因此，我們認為這筆顯著資金已對我們目前的工作及未來的機會產生正面影響，並將在接下來的十年持續產生正面影響。雖然跨黨派基礎建設投資與就業法案的資金窗口於 2026 年 9 月 30 日關閉，我們認為國會已認知基礎設施工作的長期性，並已開始立法程序以確保該日期之後的未來資金，儘管未來資金的金額與組成尚未確定。此外，關島及印度太平洋地區的多個現有專案與未來專案正由美國政府的太平洋防禦倡議計畫提供資金，該計畫提供大量多年資金，用以支持重大改善，以增強美國軍隊的基礎設施與作戰準備。

我們的建築分部在為私人與公共工程客戶提供服務方面有著豐富的經驗，服務對象包括酒店與賭場、交通、醫療、商業辦公室、政府設施、體育與娛樂、教育、監禁與拘留設施、生物科技、製藥、工業與資訊科技等專門建築市場。我們認為建築分部的成功源於我們證明過的管理與執行大型、複雜專案的能力，即使面對嚴格的快速進度、複雜的設計，以及先進的機械、電氣與生命安全系統，同時提供準確的預算與嚴格的品質控制。我們相信我們強大的聲譽、長期的客戶關係、競爭性價格與顯著的重複與推薦業務，使我們在市場上取得領導地位。
我們在酒店與賭場市場被視為領導者，專門從事高檔度假村與賭場的建設。我們與酒店經營者、原住民部落會議、開發商與建築師合作，提供多樣化的建設服務，以應對酒店與度假村新興建設與翻修的挑戰。我們認為我們在項目按時完成方面的聲譽是此市場的重要競爭優勢，因為任何專案延誤都可能導致客戶的重大收入損失。

paragraphs: 2025 年合併營業收入為 5.5 十億美元，較 2024 年的 4.3 十億美元成長 28%。本公司在 2025 年三個應報告分部均表現強勁成長，主要驅動因素為在部分較新、規模較大且毛利率較高的專案上，專案執行活動增加，所有專案均有大量工作範圍尚未完成。這些專案尚處於初期階段，預計在未來幾年將大幅增加。

2025 年建設營運收入為 232.0 百萬美元，與 2024 年建設營運虧損 103.8 百萬美元相比有顯著改善。2025 年建設營運收入增加主要由於與總體專案執行活動增加相關的貢獻，總計為 172.1 百萬美元，以及 2025 年淨不利調整金額較低，此為因各專案預計完成成本評估變動所致，包括：1) 某些專案因生產力與效率改善而產生的淨有利影響，扣除專案費用後，2025 年淨有利影響為 104.3 百萬美元，較 2024 年淨不利影響 36.4 百萬美元為高；2) 某些法律判決或決議產生的淨不利影響，2025 年總計為 32.5 百萬美元，較 2024 年 167.7 百萬美元為低；3) 2025 年暫時性總體專案調整金額為 78.7 百萬美元，較 2024 年 97.2 百萬美元為低，此為因成功協商取得較低毛利率（且較低風險）的變更契約，以及各專案未核准工作增加所致，這些暫時性對營收的影響預計在專案剩餘生命週期內會逆轉。此改善部分抵銷了各項和解對營收的淨不利影響，2025 年為 61.8 百萬美元，較 2024 年 45.8 百萬美元為高。2025 年與 2024 年因上述項目產生的重大調整，詳情請參見「應報告分部營運結果」部分。

此外，2025 年截至 12 月 31 日止，建設營運收入因股票選擇權費用 150.0 百萬美元而受到負面影響，較 2024 年的 40.4 百萬美元為高。2025 年股票選擇權費用增加主要由於本公司股票價格在 2025 年大幅上漲 176.9%，影響了負債類別獎勵的公允價值。這些負債類別獎勵在每個會計期間結算時，會按公允價值重新衡量，其變動會計入營收。這些獎勵為過去幾年因 Tutor Perini Corporation Omnibus Incentive Plan（"Plan"）下的股票池不足及低股票價格而發行的短期解決方案。本公司目前預期 2026 年股票選擇權費用將減少，2027 年將有更顯著的減少，因部分獎勵已屆滿，且大多數剩餘負債類別獎勵將在 2026 年底前屆滿。在 2025 年 5 月本公司股東批准增加 Plan 下的股票後，本公司已停止發行負債類別的長期激勵報酬獎勵，這有助於減少未來營收的波動。
2025 年的有效所得稅率為 30.0%，較 2024 年的 29.3% 為高。有關有效所得稅率變動的討論請參見下方「公司、稅務及其他事項」部分。

2025 年稀釋後每股普通股盈餘為 1.51 美元，較 2024 年稀釋後每股普通股虧損 3.13 美元為佳。2025 年調整後的稀釋每股普通股盈餘（為非 GAAP 財務指標，並排除股票選擇權費用（及相關稅務利益））為 4.29 美元，較 2024 年調整後的稀釋每股普通股虧損 2.37 美元為佳。2025 年改善主要由於上述因素導致該期間建設營運（虧損）收入的變化。有關進一步資訊及本公司根據美國通用會計準則（"GAAP"）報告的財務結果與調整後結果的對應關係，請參見下方「非 GAAP 財務指標」部分。
本公司在 2025 年產生創紀錄的營運現金流 748.1 百萬美元，主要來自較新及持續進行專案的收款，其次則為近期爭議解決相關收款。本公司在 2025 年利用部分營運現金流，自其現有 Term Loan B 債務 121.9 百萬美元中進行自願預付。

2025 年合併新契約為 7.4 十億美元，較 2024 年的 12.8 十億美元為低。Civil 與 Building 分部為 2025 年新契約活動的主要貢獻者。2025 年重大新契約及契約調整包括紐約的 Midtown Bus Terminal Replacement - Phase 1 專案 1.87 十億美元；紐約的 Manhattan Tunnel 專案 1.18 十億美元；加州價值約 1 十億美元的醫療設施專案；加州價值 538 百萬美元的醫療專案；關島 Apra Harbor Waterfront Repairs 專案額外資金 241 百萬美元；關島價值 182 百萬美元的軍事防禦專案；加州價值 155 百萬美元的教育設施專案；德克薩斯州額外資金 131 百萬美元的電力專案；以及另一個德克薩斯州價值超過 100 百萬美元的電力專案。本公司持續成功取得其應得的大型新專案機會，主要由於其戰略投標方法與有利的市場動態，包括部分較大專案在特定市場的競爭有限。此環境由強勁的公共資金與需求支撐，使本公司得以區隔自己並提出符合客戶目標與期望的有吸引力提案。本公司預期此環境將在可預見的未來持續。

2025 年 12 月 31 日合併待執行契約為 20.6 十億美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 18.7 十億美元成長 10%。2025 年 12 月 31 日，各分部待執行契約組成為 Civil 為 49%、Building 為 36%、Specialty Contractors 為 15%，較 2024 年末 Civil 為 47%、Building 為 38%、Specialty Contractors 為 15% 為高。
民營工程分部的積壓訂單中，大多數專案通常在三至五年內轉化為營業收入，而在建築及專業承包商分部則通常在一年至三年內轉化為營業收入。所有三個分部的某些較大型專案，其完成時間可能延長至更長的期間。我們估計，截至2025年12月31日的積壓訂單中，約有6十億美元，或約29%，將於2026年認列為營業收入。

headings: 與本公司業務及營運相關之風險
若我們無法準確預估契約風險、收入或成本，我們可能蒙受損失或實現低於預期之利潤。
我們之契約常要求我們執行超出初始專案範疇之工作，這可能會導致爭議或聲請，並對我們之營運資金、利潤及現金流產生不利影響。
經濟因素，例如通貨膨脹、關稅、新契約授獎時間或專案執行速度，已導致並可能繼續導致損失或低於預期之利潤。
我們之實際結果可能與用以編製財務報表之預估及假設不同。
若總體經濟條件出現顯著減速或衰退，例如在衰退時期所呈現之情形，可能會對我們之營運產生不利影響。
建設服務業高度依賴排程，若我們未能符合契約之排程要求，可能會對我們之聲譽產生不利影響，並使我們面臨財務責任。
聯邦、州及地方政府對基礎建設及其他公共專案之支出減少或延遲，可能會對我們未來可參與之專案數量產生不利影響。
資訊科技系統中斷及資料安全與/或隱私權遭入侵，可能不利於我們的營運能力，並對我們的營運成果造成負面影響。
天氣狀況及其他非我們所能控制的事件，可能顯著影響我們的營業收入與獲利能力。
我們面臨與政府契約（包括政府停擺及經費考量）及相關採購法規有關的風險。
我們的國際營運使我們面臨經濟、政治、法規及其他風險，以及與美國政府經費相關的不確定性，可能對我們的營業收入與獲利造成不利影響。
我們參與建設合資企業，可能因合作夥伴的失敗而使我們承擔責任或損害我們的聲譽。
我們可能無法完全實現背書中所報告的收入價值，因取消或減縮範圍，包括因政府相關命令所致。
新項目獎勵的競爭非常激烈，我們若無法有效競爭，可能降低我們的市佔率與利潤。
我們可能因違反美國外國腐敗行為防治法及類似全球反賄賂法規而受到不利影響。
公共衛生危機，例如 COVID-19，已對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成負面影響，未來亦可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成負面影響。
與氣候變遷相關的實體及法規風險，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大負面影響。
與我們資本結構相關的風險
無法取得擔保可能對我們的營運及營運成果產生負面影響。
我們擁有大量負債，且負債條款具有限制性，這可能會對我們的財務狀況產生負面影響，並可能使我們無法履行債務協議中的義務。
我們信用評級的降級可能對我們的業務及財務狀況造成重大負面影響。
與我們股票持有相關的風險
我們的執行 chairman 由於其職位及重大股權利益，可能對本公司產生影響力。
一般風險因素
本公司普通股的市價可能有顯著波動，這可能會導致股東遭受重大損失並使本公司成為訴訟對象。
本公司無法保證普通股的股息發放時間、金額或支付，亦無法保證本公司將根據股息回購計畫回購普通股。
paragraphs: 本公司面臨許多已知及未知的風險與不確定性，這些風險與不確定性可能對本公司營運造成重大不利影響。下列為可能導致本公司實際結果與本報告內所含之預測性陳述有所差異，並可能對本公司財務狀況、營運結果與現金流造成重大不利影響之重大風險與不確定性說明，並於本報告其他部分亦有說明。
與合約相關之收入與成本會計處理，需管理階層做出重大之估計與假設，這些估計與假設可能在專案生命週期中大幅變動，此情形過去已導致，且未來可能導致，對本公司合併財務報表造成重大影響。此外，成本超支，包括固定價格合約與保證最高價格合約中未預見的成本增加，過去已導致，且未來可能導致，利潤減少或虧損。
本公司參與許多法律程序，若這些程序對本公司不利，可能對本公司財務結果與/或現金流造成不利影響，損害本公司聲譽與/或使本公司無法參與未來專案。本公司亦可能在法律程序進行中投入大量營運資金於專案上。

本公司參與多項訴訟，包括於財務報表附註第 8 項所述之法律程序。訴訟本質上具有不確定性，且無法準確預測任何法律程序之最終結果。本公司必須做出某些假設並依賴估計，這些假設與估計本質上具有風險與不確定性，以決定適當之或有負債與對營業收入之衝擊。任何與本公司預期與估計顯著不同之不利法律程序結果或和解，可能對本公司財務狀況、營運結果與現金流造成重大不利影響。此可能包括要求本公司記錄費用或減少先前已記錄之收入，或要求本公司支付賠償金或減少預期可收取之現金。例如，於 2024 年 10 月，本公司收到一項與已完成之加州民事工程專案相關之遺留爭議之意外不利仲裁裁決，導致非現金費用 101.6 百萬美元，本公司正提出上訴。此外，任何未來之不利判決可能損害本公司聲譽，並對本公司未來獲取專案之能力造成負面影響。
本公司可能對專案所有者提出聲請，要求補償超出合約價格之額外費用或合約價格中未包含之金額。當這些類型事件發生且未解決之聲請仍在進行中時，本公司可能為覆蓋成本超支而投入大量營運資金於專案上。未能迅速回收這些聲請之金額，過去已對本公司流動性與財務結果造成重大不利影響，且未來可能繼續造成重大不利影響，並可能導致進一步之法律程序。
本公司之合約常要求本公司執行超出初始專案範疇之工作，即使客戶未事先同意該工作範疇與/或價格。此過程過去已導致，且未來可能導致，爭議或聲請，關於執行之工作是否超出客戶指示之範疇與/或超出客戶願意支付之價格，此已導致過去出現重大現金流限制。若本公司無法回收此工作之成本，或因不利之訴訟或仲裁結果或和解中接受低於預期之金額而延遲回收這些成本，本公司之營運資金、利潤與現金流已受到與可能繼續受到不利影響。
